question: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, allows juveniles aged 16-18 to be tried as adults in cases of:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: theft
drug abuse
cybercrime
heinous crimes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is heinous crimes

Explanation:
Under Sections 15 and 18 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, juveniles aged 16-18 can be tried as adults for heinous offences. Heinous offences are those punishable with minimum imprisonment of seven years. The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) assesses whether the juvenile understood the nature and consequences of the offence. If so, the case may be transferred to a children's court or regular court. Theft, drug abuse, and cybercrime are not automatically heinous unless they carry a minimum seven-year sentence. This provision balances rehabilitation with accountability for serious crimes, ensuring that young offenders are not automatically treated as adults but can be when the crime is grave. The Act aims to reform juveniles while delivering justice in severe cases.

☛ Who transfers the case to adult court? → JJB

question: In which of the following years was Delhi Metro Rail Corporation established?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: When was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) established to investigate cases of human rights violations in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

10 December 1994
15 January 1995
20 February 1996
solution:

Explanation:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It is a statutory body that investigates cases of human rights violations in India. The commission consists of a chairperson (a former Chief Justice of India) and four members. question: Which of the following is a private sector organisation in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: The foreign exchange crisis forced India to seek external support. Which institution provided India a loan during the 1991 crisis?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: ADB
World Bank
WTO
IMF
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is IMF

Explanation:
In 1991, India faced a severe foreign exchange crisis, with forex reserves sufficient for only two weeks of imports. To tackle this crisis, the Indian government sought a loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The IMF provided an emergency loan of $2.2 billion to India, subject to conditions such as economic reforms and liberalization. This loan helped India overcome the forex crisis and paved the way for economic reforms. While the World Bank and ADB also provided loans later, the initial loan in 1991 was from the IMF. The WTO is a global trade organization and does not provide loans.

question_hi: राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन (FRBM) अधिनियम ने राजकोषीय घाटे और सार्वजनिक ऋण पर सीमाएं निर्धारित कीं। मूल FRBM अधिनियम के तहत 2008-09 तक राजकोषीय घाटे का लक्ष्य क्या था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: जीडीपी का 4.5%
जीडीपी का 5%
जीडीपी का 6%
जीडीपी का 3%
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जीडीपी का 3%

Explanation:
मूल FRBM अधिनियम, 2003 के अनुसार, सरकार को 2008-09 तक राजकोषीय घाटे को जीडीपी के 3% तक लाना था। यह अधिनियम वित्तीय अनुशासन सुनिश्चित करने और राजकोषीय स्थिरता बढ़ाने के उद्देश्य से बनाया गया था। इसके तहत राजकोषीय घाटे और सार्वजनिक ऋण पर लक्ष्य निर्धारित किए गए। बाद में वैश्विक वित्तीय संकट के कारण लक्ष्य को स्थगित किया गया। वर्तमान में FRBM अधिनियम को NK सिंह समिति की सिफारिशों के अनुसार संशोधित किया गया है, जिसमें 2023 तक राजकोषीय घाटे को जीडीपी के 3% पर लाने का लक्ष्य है।
